issue.title: Flaky: test_agents_slow_tool_calls_fold_levels_png_snapshots fails only under full parallel suite
issue.description:
Discovered while verifying the sase-cu fix (unrelated flaky clipboard-modal test). Ran 'just test' three times in a row on an otherwise clean workspace to confirm the sase-cu fix held under xdist contention. On one of the three runs, this PNG visual-snapshot test failed:

  tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_slow_tools.py::test_agents_slow_tool_calls_fold_levels_png_snapshots

It did not fail on the other two full-suite runs, and was not re-verified in isolation before filing (out of scope for sase-cu, which is specifically about the artifact-file clipboard-copy modal test). Given the visual snapshot suite's known sensitivity to renderer/font timing and CPU contention (see just/CLAUDE.md notes on `.pytest_cache/sase-visual/` artifacts and the CI ratio-only drift tolerance), this may be resource-contention-driven rendering nondeterminism under xdist rather than a real regression — worth someone re-running the dedicated visual suite (`just test-visual`) under load and inspecting `.pytest_cache/sase-visual/` actual/expected/diff artifacts to confirm before concluding it's a timing flake vs. a real snapshot drift.

payload.close_reason: I think we already fixed this.

evidence.note: Independent recurrence on 2026-08-05 at master 5daa94ff7 + local sase-f0 bead-conflict changes. Full 'just check' (pytest -n 4) failed exactly two nodes: tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_slow_tools.py::test_agents_slow_tool_calls_fold_levels_png_snapshots and tests/test_bead/test_cli_work_contention_regressions.py::test_concurrent_bead_mutations_wait_past_the_old_lock_timeout - the same pair sase-e9 recorded. Both passed immediately in isolation (slow-tools visual 8.77s, bead contention 3.66s call vs 52.74s under load), and a clean full 'just test-visual' passed 407/407 on rerun after one earlier full-visual run failed only this node. Caveat on load: a second full 'just check' for an unrelated workspace (sase_14) was running concurrently on the same host, so this is oversubscription rather than idle-host nondeterminism. Changed code is confined to bead event-stream conflict resolution and touches no TUI rendering.

payload.entry:
Verified at master 7ba83b1e1: the named test (test_agents_slow_tool_calls_fold_levels_png_snapshots) is NOT a real regression — it is resource-contention-driven rendering/wait-timeout nondeterminism, matching the bead's hypothesis.

Evidence:
- `just test-visual -- tests/.../test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_slow_tools.py`: 1 passed in 8.48s (clean isolation baseline).
- Two independent full runs of `SASE_VISUAL_CONTENTION_WORKERS=18 just test-visual-contention` (taskset -c 0,1, 2-CPU-pinned oversubscription, 407 items each): the named test passed cleanly both times. Each run produced exactly 1 failure out of 407, but a DIFFERENT visual test each time — test_agents_lane_neighbors_above_sase_context_png_snapshot (538.87s run), then test_agents_collapsed_panel_png_snapshot (496.18s run). Both failures were `AssertionError: Timed out after 15.00s waiting for ...` (an SVG-sentinel wait, then a footer-state wait) with no `.pytest_cache/sase-visual/` diff artifact produced for either — i.e. genuine async-wait timeouts under CPU contention, not pixel/content drift.
- This "whack-a-mole, different node each contention run, passes cleanly in isolation" signature is the same shape already tracked by umbrella task sase-ct, which the owner closed today (2026-08-05T19:19:38Z) as canceled: "This is an old bead. Let's not re-open this." Per that explicit direction, I did not file a new follow-up task or +1 sase-ct for this recurrence — recording the evidence here instead since sase-cx itself wasn't part of that consolidation (it was in_progress/reserved to me at triage time).

Conclusion: no code change needed for this bead's named test; closing as confirmed timing flake under genuine host contention, consistent with prior EVIDENCE entries from sase-e9 and sase-f0 on this same bead.

evidence.note: Independent post-close recurrence on 2026-08-13 while verifying unrelated Artifacts split-mode UI work. The exact node tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_slow_tools.py::test_agents_slow_tool_calls_fold_levels_png_snapshots timed out waiting for the loaded tools footer in the full just test-visual run, in a two-node focused rerun, and again with SASE_PYTEST_WORKERS=1. The serial run reached active_section_identity == slow-tool-calls but the footer stayed '○ tools' for the entire 15s semantic wait. This is now deterministic in isolation on a tree containing sase-cx's prior close, not merely host-contention drift. The current diff only adds Artifacts split sizing, badge, keymap actions, docs, and snapshots; it does not touch Agents prompt panels, slow-tool sources, or footer selection.

payload.close_reason: Fixed by 72f93fb1f 'fix: stabilize visual closeout and verification gates' (2026-08-21), which added semantic readiness waits for the agents frames. tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_slow_tools.py replaced wait_for_visual_idle with wait_for_state on _slow_tool_section_and_footer_ready (active slow-tool section plus populated footer) before each capture, so the snapshot no longer races an unconverged render. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
